Repeat for the other shifts. *Daily cadence* | Shift | Observations per day | |-------|----------------------| | Day | 2–3 (over 8‑hour shift) | | Evening | 1–2 (over 6‑hour shift) | | Night | 0–1 (over 4‑hour shift) | *Auditor rotation* - **Auditor A** covers the first half of each shift, - **Auditor B** covers the second half. Both auditors alternate days so that each nurse is observed by both auditors over a month. --- **2. What an auditor must record for every observation** | Field | Description | Why it matters | |-------|-------------|----------------| | **Date & Time** | Exact timestamp of the hand‑hygiene event. | Enables trend analysis and shift‑specific compliance. | | **Shift** | Day / Evening / Night. | Correlates compliance with staffing patterns. | | **Nurse ID (or badge number)** | Unique identifier. | Allows individual performance tracking without compromising anonymity. | | **Patient Identifier** | Patient MRN or bedside code. | Confirms that the observation is patient‑directed and not a “clean‑room” event. | | **WHO Moment (1–5)** | 1: Before touching a patient, 2: Before clean/aseptic procedure, 3: After body fluid exposure risk, 4: After touching a patient, 5: After contact with patient surroundings. | Ensures all five moments are covered and identifies weak points. | | **Action Taken** | Hand‑rub (alcohol gel) or hand‑wash (soap & water). | Distinguishes between product types and compliance rates per method. | | **Duration** | Seconds spent on the hand‑hygiene action. | Checks whether the minimum 20 s is met. | | **Compliance?** | Yes / No. | Core metric for audit. | | **If Non‑Compliant – Reason** | e.g., “No product available”, “Time pressure”, “Forgot”. | Drives targeted interventions. | | **Environmental Context** | Brief note on location (e.g., bedside, procedure room) and any barrier to compliance (crowding, equipment). | Helps explain patterns beyond individual behavior. | *Validation checklist* - Observation must be witnessed in real‑time (no video or retrospective review). - All fields above must be filled; missing data renders the observation invalid. - Auditors sign off on each completed sheet. --- **3.
